name: Lavender & Bergamot
description: Calming and stabilizing blend for anxiety reduction and improved sleep quality.
scientific_prove_reference: Lavender increased theta and alpha EEG activity (relaxation) (Sayorwan et al., 2012; Table 2). Bergamot with music increased relaxation (Peng et al., 2009; Table 2). Mixture more effective than lavender alone (Lee, 2016; Table 2).

name: Peppermint & Eucalyptus
description: Invigorating and alertness-enhancing scent for cognitive performance and physical energy.
scientific_prove_reference: Peppermint enhanced memory and alertness, increased running speed and push-ups (Moss et al., 2008; Raudenbush et al., 2001; Table 3). Eucalyptus reduced pain and blood pressure post-surgery (Jun et al., 2013; Table 3).

name: Rosemary & Lemon
description: Stimulating and memory-enhancing fragrance for mental clarity and reduced fatigue.
scientific_prove_reference: Rosemary increased alertness by decreasing frontal alpha and beta EEG (Diego et al., 1998; Table 2) and enhanced memory performance (Moss et al., 2003; Table 3). Lemon and lavender reduced stress during VDT tasks (Kawakami et al., 1999; Table 2).

name: Ylang-Ylang & Sandalwood
description: Sensual and deeply relaxing scent for stress relief and mood elevation.
scientific_prove_reference: Ylang-ylang decreased blood pressure, increased skin temperature, and increased calmness (Hongratanaworakit & Buchbauer, 2006; Table 3). Sandalwood (awakening) and lavender (sedative) improved productivity (Kawakami et al., 1999; Table 2).

name: Jasmine & Rose
description: Uplifting and romantic fragrance for positive mood, well-being, and reduced anxiety.
scientific_prove_reference: Jasmine increased beta wave activity in anterior/left posterior regions and feelings of well-being (Sayowan et al., 2013; Table 2). Rose oil decreased relative sympathetic activity (Haze et al., 2002; Table 3).

name: Sweet Orange & Neroli
description: Cheerful and anxiolytic citrus blend for reducing state anxiety and improving mood.
scientific_prove_reference: Orange odor reduced anxiety and increased calmness in women (Lehrner et al., 2000; Table 3). Neroli and grapefruit oils increased slow alpha and theta EEG, promoting a relaxed state (Iijima et al., 2007; Table 2).

name: Chamomile & Clary Sage
description: Gentle sedative and soothing scent for stress reduction and improved sleep.
scientific_prove_reference: Chamomile (Roman) had sedative effects and increased subjective calmness (Moss et al., 2006; Table 3). Chamomile and eugenol decreased alpha1 EEG, correlated with comfort (Masago et al., 2000; Table 2).

name: Grapefruit & Lemon
description: Refreshing and revitalizing scent for reducing cortical deactivation and promoting alertness.
scientific_prove_reference: Grapefruit oil increased slow alpha and theta EEG in occipital region, reducing cortical deactivation (Iijima et al., 2007; Table 2). Lemon, lavender, sandalwood improved productivity and reduced stress (Kawakami et al., 1999; Table 2).

name: Cinnamon & Clove
description: Warm and confidence-boosting spice blend for focus and reduced mental fatigue.
scientific_prove_reference: Cinnamon and clove (eugenol) decreased alpha1 EEG, correlated with comfort (Masago et al., 2000; Table 2). Spicy/warm scents associated with higher dominance and confidence (ANEW: 'powerful' V:0.68, A:0.73, D:0.91).

name: Sandalwood & Cedarwood
description: Grounding and meditative woody scent for stability, reflection, and inner strength.
scientific_prove_reference: Sandalwood (sedative) improved work concentration (Kawakami et al., 1999; Table 2). Woody scents associated with low arousal, high dominance, and calm focus (ANEW: 'peace' V:0.84, A:0.24, D:0.56; 'quiet' V:0.57, A:0.23, D:0.43).

name: Spearmint & Tea Tree
description: Cooling and clarifying blend for mental focus and decongestive freshness.
scientific_prove_reference: Spearmint (in GEOS) associated with refreshment and revitalization (Chrea et al., 2009). Tea tree (Melaleuca) used in aromatherapy for psychological disorders (Ali et al., 2015; Table 1).

name: Frankincense & Myrrh
description: Meditative and grounding resinous scent for spiritual calm and introspection.
scientific_prove_reference: Incense (olibanum/frankincense) increased fast alpha activity in bilateral posterior regions, enhancing cortical inhibitory processing (Iijima et al., 2009; Table 2).

name: Vanilla & Sandalwood
description: Sweet, comforting, and nostalgic fragrance for warmth and emotional security.
scientific_prove_reference: Vanilla odor (real food) reduced theta EEG activity, indicating reduced attention load and increased comfort (Martin, 1998; Table 2). Sandalwood provides grounding woody base.

name: Cypress & Juniper
description: Forest-fresh and purifying scent for post-exercise recovery and mental reset.
scientific_prove_reference: Cypress produced favorable impression after physical work (Sugawara et al., 1999; Table 3). Juniper created favorable impression after mental work (Sugawara et al., 1999; Table 3).

name: Lemongrass & Geranium
description: Uplifting and balancing citrus-herbal blend for stress reduction and mood elevation.
scientific_prove_reference: Geranium oil inhalation lowered state and trait anxiety scores (Morris et al., 1995; Table 3). Lemongrass (Cymbopogon citratus) contains citral (geranial) with stimulating properties (Table 1).

name: Patchouli & Bergamot
description: Earthy yet bright scent for grounding and emotional balance, reducing sympathetic overactivity.
scientific_prove_reference: Patchouli oil decreased relative sympathetic activity by 40% (Haze et al., 2002; Table 3). Bergamot with music increased relaxation (Peng et al., 2009; Table 2).

name: Thyme & Oregano
description: Herbaceous and protective scent for mental clarity and immune-supporting comfort.
scientific_prove_reference: Thyme and oregano (carvacrol, thymol) are major components in essential oils used for psychological disorders (Ali et al., 2015; Table 1). High dominance associated with protective herbs (ANEW: 'strong' V:0.78, A:0.65, D:0.85).

name: Neroli & Clary Sage
description: Floral-herbal relaxant for reducing anxiety and promoting restorative sleep.
scientific_prove_reference: Neroli oil increased slow alpha and theta EEG in occipital region, reducing cortical deactivation (Iijima et al., 2007; Table 2). Clary sage (Salvia sclarea) used for insomnia and stress (Ali et al., 2015; Table 1).

name: Cardamom & Cinnamon
description: Warm, spicy, and invigorating blend for focus and social confidence.
scientific_prove_reference: Cinnamon (cinnamaldehyde) major component in essential oils (Table 1). Spicy scents associated with high arousal and dominance (ANEW: 'powerful' A:0.73, D:0.91).

name: Basil & Peppermint
description: Sharp, cooling, and mentally sharpening scent for sustained attention and alertness.
scientific_prove_reference: Basil (Ocimum basilicum) major component linalool (Table 1). Peppermint enhanced memory and alertness, reduced sleepiness (Moss et al., 2008; Norrish & Dwyer, 2005; Table 3).

name: Rose & Geranium
description: Floral heart blend for self-compassion, emotional warmth, and reduced irritability.
scientific_prove_reference: Rose oil decreased relative sympathetic activity by 40% (Haze et al., 2002; Table 3). Geranium lowered anxiety (Morris et al., 1995; Table 3). Combined floral notes enhance positive mood.

name: Eucalyptus & Rosemary
description: Medicinal, clear-headed blend for respiratory ease and cognitive sharpness.
scientific_prove_reference: Eucalyptus (1,8-cineole) correlated with cognitive performance following rosemary aroma exposure (Moss & Oliver, 2012; Table 3). Rosemary increased alertness (Diego et al., 1998; Table 2).

name: Lime & Ylang-Ylang
description: Bright tropical-floral scent for mood lifting and mild sedative relaxation.
scientific_prove_reference: Lime (Citrus) shares properties with lemon and grapefruit: increased alpha/theta and reduced stress (Iijima et al., 2007; Table 2). Ylang-ylang increased calmness (Hongratanaworakit & Buchbauer, 2006; Table 3).

name: Vetiver & Lavender
description: Deep, smoky-herbal grounding for severe anxiety and overthinking.
scientific_prove_reference: Lavender increased theta and alpha EEG, reducing mental stress (Sayorwan et al., 2012; Motomura et al., 2001; Table 2 & 3). Vetiver (Chrysopogon zizanioides) traditionally used for grounding; low arousal consistent with ANEW 'peace'.

name: Black Pepper & Ginger
description: Spicy, warming, and energizing scent for physical vitality and motivation.
scientific_prove_reference: Black pepper oil increased relative sympathetic activity (Haze et al., 2002; Table 3). Ginger (Zingiber) related to energizing spices. High arousal and dominance from ANEW 'excited' (V:0.80, A:0.83, D:0.77).

name: Heliotropin & Vanilla
description: Sweet, powdery, and sleep-enhancing aroma for insomnia relief and nighttime calm.
scientific_prove_reference: Heliotropin (aromatic compound) reduced sleepiness and improved refreshment at awakening for insomnia sufferers (Yamagishi et al., 2010; Table 3). Vanilla reduces theta EEG, indicating relaxed attention (Martin, 1998; Table 2).

name: Galaxolide & Musk
description: Clean, subtle, and undetected-but-effective scent for divided attention and background calm.
scientific_prove_reference: Galaxolide (synthetic musk) produced significant alpha EEG differences even when undetected, suggesting odors affect CNS activity without conscious perception (Lorig et al., 1991; Table 2).

name: Linalool & Linalyl Acetate
description: Pure lavender-derived terpenes for precise sedative and mood-stabilizing effects.
scientific_prove_reference: (RS)-(±)-linalool significantly decreased beta wave activity after work, indicating sedation (Sugawara et al., 1998; Table 2). Linalyl acetate is major component in lavender (Table 1).

name: Limonene & Terpinolene
description: Citrus-terpene blend for gender-differentiated relaxation and stabilization.
scientific_prove_reference: Terpinolene increased relative fast alpha in right prefrontal region, reducing tension and increasing relaxation (Sowndhararajan et al., 2015; Table 2). (+)-Limonene increased fast alpha more in women than men (same reference).

name: Cedarwood & Juniper
description: Dry, woody, and meditative blend for mental endurance and emotional resilience.
scientific_prove_reference: Juniper (Juniperus sps.) major components bornyl acetate, sabinene, α-pinene (Table 1). Juniper created favorable impression after mental work (Sugawara et al., 1999; Table 3). Low arousal woody scents from ANEW 'quiet'.

name: Peppermint & Jasmine
description: Bright, euphoric and awakening blend for high-energy joy, motivation and social lift.
scientific_prove_reference: Peppermint increased alertness (Moss et al., 2008; Table 3) and was rated more pleasant, stimulating and elating than water (Goel & Lau, 2006; Table 3). Jasmine increased beta EEG activity, linked to feelings of well-being, activity and freshness (Sayowan et al., 2013; Table 2). Jasmine and peppermint were both classed as awakening fragrances (Kawakami et al., 1999; Table 2). VAD anchored on ANEW (Bradley & Lang, 1999): 'excitement' V:0.81, A:0.83, D:0.65; 'thrill' V:0.88, A:0.88, D:0.69; 'joy' V:0.95, A:0.78, D:0.66 (mean V:0.88, A:0.83, D:0.67).

name: Roman Chamomile & Heliotropin
description: Hushed, sheltering and sedative blend for deep rest and for feeling looked after.
scientific_prove_reference: Roman chamomile had a sedative effect; subjective calmness was linked to that effect and to arousal expectancy (Moss et al., 2006; Table 3). Heliotropin reduced sleepiness and improved refreshment at awakening in insomnia sufferers (Yamagishi et al., 2010; Table 3). Dominance below 0.50 is a design assumption: the ANEW manual describes low dominance as feeling 'cared-for', 'controlled' or 'guided', and no study measured dominance for these aromas. VAD anchored on ANEW (Bradley & Lang, 1999): 'quiet' V:0.57, A:0.23, D:0.43; 'sheltered' V:0.59, A:0.41, D:0.34 (mean V:0.58, A:0.32, D:0.39).
